newsitem.title: USA: Oversight board spurns Miami bailout plan.
newsitem.headline: Oversight board spurns Miami bailout plan.

text.p: A state-appointed oversight board on Tuesday rejected Miami's deficit-cutting proposal, saying some revenue estimates were doubtful.
The board also said that the city needs to build up $13.6 million, or 20 percent of its $68 million annual budget deficit, as a financial cushion against uncollected funds or emergencies.
The city will have until Jan 25 to submit a revised proposal.
Lt. Gov. Buddy McKay, who chairs the oversight board, said $9.9 million of the revenues in the city's $68 million bailout plan were "too iffy" to consider as solid revenues.
The questionable revenues included overdue garbage-service fees and federal grants to police departments which are still pending in Congress.
The board's only option was to accept or reject the entire plan. However, board members said that at least 85 percent of the plan seemed acceptable.
"I think we are close," board member Robert Baetty said.
Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles appointed the board to guide Miami's fiscal recovery last month.
The $68 million deficit in its $275 million budget for the city which began October 1 came to light after three top city officials resigned to face federal corruption charges.
